artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Source change only; the release is OG-r-1's. Every OAuth record now goes through app/access_state.py (OG-d-1): clients RUNTIME#client#<id>; pending authorizations RUNTIME#pending_auth#<arid> (600 s, nonce-bound); codes RUNTIME#code#<sha256> (60 s, single use); refresh families RUNTIME#refresh#<fid> plus one record per generation #g<n> (tokens stored only as SHA-256; one conditional transaction per rotation; reuse revokes; 30 d absolute / 7 d idle). Access tokens 900 s with an fid claim. principal_key() is the one function OG-a-2 changes. The stateless JWT refresh functions are removed (row NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S3).

Source change only. /register accepts JSON only and /token form encoding only; register, authorize, callback and token run their blocking work on a dedicated pool under the C1 budgets (oauth_as.AUTH_ENDPOINT_SECONDS 10, REFRESH_ENDPOINT_SECONDS 30) and answer 503 when a budget elapses; the callback resumes the durable pending authorization before it asks the upstream for the identity; OAuth route paths come from oauth_as constants.

New file: test_oga1_ac01 .. test_oga1_ac18, one per criterion. The tests are offline: moto 5.2.3 sits behind a per-request lock that models DynamoDB's request serialization, the upstream identity provider is a local issuer with an RSA key generated at test time, the Fernet key is generated at test time, and fake AWS credentials plus an empty config are forced. The HTTP arms drive the real Starlette app in-process. Each test prints its denominator line. The fixture restores the builtin time.monotonic that tests/test_ratelimit.py replaces process-wide (row NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S6).

Four rows appended (NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S3 .. W3-S6), committed on their own before this proof: '[surprise-row-gate] ... 4 new row(s) of 8 total checked (4 pre-existing, NOT re-graded)' and 'OK: 1 file(s), all new rows carry their step-7/step-10 fields.'

declared_exclusions.item: The live access-state table, its IAM LeadingKeys grant and a real DynamoDB round trip.
declared_exclusions.reason: OG-i-1's cell. Every criterion here runs offline against moto 5.2.3, as the order specifies. The attribute names the adapter uses must match OG-i-1's table (row NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S1, ARMED, from the previous order).

declared_exclusions.item: The immutable tid/oid principal, legacy access-JWT rejection on protected routes, the family-status check on every protected request, the inventory of registered clients and the one-time reconnect notice.
declared_exclusions.reason: OG-a-2's cell (the order: 'The immutable principal (tid/oid) and the legacy cutover are the NEXT cell's'). This cell binds families through principal_key() and puts the family id in each access token (fid claim) for that cell to check. The legacy REFRESH refusal already lands here (row NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S3).

declared_exclusions.item: An HTTP logout or token-revocation endpoint.
declared_exclusions.reason: No criterion names one and no such route exists today. Family revocation is revoke_family(); the existing operator kill path (revocation lists, by family id and by user cutoff or blocklist) revokes a family at its next refresh. A new public route would widen the ALB and rate-limit surface beyond this order.

declared_exclusions.item: A restart across two operating-system processes.
declared_exclusions.reason: AC13/AC14 simulate the restart in-process: a new adapter and client over the same table, plus an AST assertion that oauth_as.py holds no process-local store. A two-process test needs a DynamoDB endpoint that outlives a process; moto's server mode needs flask, which is not installed in .venv-og, and the order grants no dependency change.

declared_exclusions.item: Removing the dead GATEWAY_TOKEN_TTL / GATEWAY_REFRESH_TTL keys from config.py, and scoping test_ratelimit.py's process-wide clock patch.
declared_exclusions.reason: Both files are outside this order's <paths> grant, and the order forbids editing existing tests. Rows NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S4 and NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S6.
Forbidden by the order; the release is OG-r-1's. Every commit is LOCAL on branch wk-nfra_oplgtw-1-3b; the COO drains it.

surprises: NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S3: OG-a-1's durable refresh route cannot keep the stateless JWT refresh branch without breaking C1's no-stateless-branch rule, so it already refuses every pre-durable refresh token with invalid_grant, a refusal the decomposition gives to OG-a-2's legacy cutover. OBSERVATION, INERT.

NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S4: token lifetimes now come from the contract's limits, which leaves config.py's GATEWAY_TOKEN_TTL / GATEWAY_REFRESH_TTL declared but read by nothing; config.py is outside the grant. OBSERVATION, INERT.
NFRA_OPLGTW-W3-S5: C1 names no lifetime for a client record; every Dynamic Client Registration is stored without expiry, bounded only by the per-IP auth rate limit. OBSERVATION, INERT.
